details:
A WhatsApp (Baileys-derived) library carrying hidden, install-adjacent automation that enrols every connected account into attacker-chosen WhatsApp channels.

In lib/Socket/socket.js a URL is stored as a decimal char-code array and rebuilt at run time with String.fromCharCode(..._u), yielding hxxps://raw[.]github[.]com/skyzopedia/NewsletterID/refs/heads/main/VIP_Push[.]json (a non-standard raw[.]github[.]com host, not the GitHub raw-content host). This runs unconditionally from the socket connect path: fetchLatestBaileysVersion() executes socketConnect(), which fetches the list before the handshake completes and then, inside a 200-second setTimeout, sends one w:mex IQ query per entry with query_id 7871414976211147 (the newsletter FOLLOW query, defined as QueryIds.FOLLOW in lib/Types/Newsletter.js) and variables.newsletter_id taken from the remote list. All errors are swallowed, so the account joins each channel silently.

A second hidden path in the same file, generateMessageV(n) (exported to callers via the socket object), decodes the base64 constant "JCUkJCQjIyQkIyMjIyQjIyMjIyQjIyMjQG5ld3NsZXR0ZXI=" and XORs each character with key 23, producing 120363405765232446@newsletter, then after a 40-second timer calls the same FOLLOW query for that fixed channel, again inside a try/catch that discards failures. Both channels are attacker-controlled: the second is fixed in the code, the first is whatever the remote JSON contains.

A separate auto-follow module (lib/Channels/index.js, exported from the entry point) fetches config/channels.json from an account-controlled raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com path and follows every channel ID listed there on connection open; that remote list is mutable after publication.

Indicators: hxxps://raw[.]github[.]com/skyzopedia/NewsletterID/refs/heads/main/VIP_Push[.]json; hxxps://raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com/ardanClv/ardanbaileys/main/config/channels[.]json; hardcoded channel 120363405765232446; newsletter FOLLOW query id 7871414976211147; decoder key 23 in lib/Socket/socket.js.
